text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Top government officials met on the directives of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to chalk out a plan for the transportation of imported wheat being offloaded at the Karachi port to avoid any shortages during the Moslem festival of Eid al-Adha.
- An activist of breakaway faction of ethnic Mohajir National Movement was killed by unidentified assailants and bodies of two men with torture marks were found in Karachi.
- Two Indians including a child were killed and eight were wounded as Pakistan and Indian troops traded fire on the line of control for the third day in a row.
- The federal government plans to downsize the existing 1,032 state-run organisations and corporations within the next two to three weeks, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- The government plans to cut vegoil imports to half in the next two years by increasing domestic production, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.
- Pakistan said it was ready to continue talks with India despite change of government in New Dehli.
- Pakistan's Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan is expected to go to the United States on May 19.
- Pakistan plans to build nine motorways and additional roads at a cost of 146.7 billion rupees to prepare the country to enter the next century.
